 Jensen Huang Rumored to Have Had Romantic Relationship with Chinese Spy... Controversy Grows
 Kim Jeong-gi 
 Seoul 
 Published 
 2026.11.08 11:36 
 View 
 View Count 
 PIP 닫기 
 [Anchor] 
 Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang, a leading figure in the global semiconductor industry, has become embroiled in allegations that he was in a romantic relationship with a Chinese spy. The controversy is escalating as it leads to efforts by the U.S. Congress to uncover the truth. 
 Reporter Kim Jeong-gi has the details. 
 [Reporter] 
 At a dinner gathering of big tech executives held in Taiwan last year. 
 A woman in pink warmly greets Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. 
 After dinner, they leave together in the same car. 
 The woman is Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. 
 However, successive reports have emerged stating that U.S. intelligence agencies suspect this woman is a Chinese spy and have concluded that she was in a romantic relationship with Jensen Huang. 
 The Financial Times reported that U.S. intelligence agencies drafted a memo detailing the relationship between the two based on intelligence secured earlier this year. 
 The New York Times also reported on the U.S. intelligence assessment that China attempted to gather information on Jensen Huang through Alice Huang and exert influence to have Nvidia supply cutting-edge semiconductors to China. 
 [Paul Mozur / Global Tech Correspondent, The New York Times: U.S. intelligence agencies view her as an intelligence asset for the Chinese government. In other words, she is passing information to Beijing.] 
 Megaspeed, the company Alice Huang was affiliated with, has been under investigation by U.S. authorities over suspicions of smuggling advanced Nvidia semiconductors into China while evading U.S. export controls. 
 Nvidia stated that the contact between the two was routine business interaction and that its own investigation found no evidence of wrongdoing. 
 However, with the U.S. Congress summoning Jensen Huang to directly explain his relationship with Alice Huang, the fallout is expected to continue spreading. 
 (Video Editing: Jeon Min-gyu)
